title: Separate contracted campus capacity from operating cash flow
prompt: Build the project-state view for Polaris Forge 1 at the cutoff. Reconcile signed customer capacity, building-level operating status, secured construction debt, and the evidence still needed for land, power, delivery, and revenue timing. Report only.

observations.content: Three executed long-term customer leases cover 400 MW at the campus over approximately 15-year base terms, with about $11.0 billion described as total contracted revenue over those base terms.

The first 100 MW building is operating. A second 150 MW building is only partially operating, and a third 150 MW building remains under construction with anticipated service readiness in 2027. The portfolio disclosure says only about 100 MW at the campus was operating and revenue-generating at the reporting date.

A project subsidiary issued $2.35 billion of 9.25% senior secured notes due in 2030 at 97% of principal. Proceeds fund only a portion of construction and related expenses for the first two buildings, repay an earlier loan, fund debt-service reserves, and pay transaction expenses. Interest is payable semiannually beginning in June 2026.

The portfolio category says each contracted operating-or-under-construction megawatt is backed by land under company control and/or an executed utility power agreement. The disjunctive portfolio statement does not identify both land and power evidence for every individual building.

Expected delivery dates are management estimates and remain subject to construction, permitting, interconnection, and other risks. Contracted base-term revenue is therefore not the same as current-period revenue or cash.

oracle.terminal_when: The report separates executed backlog from building-level operation and revenue, preserves restricted debt uses, and does not turn a land-or-power portfolio statement into proof of both rights.

title: Link phased rent to delivery, debt, and construction-cost controls
prompt: Assess Black Pearl at the cutoff as a financed but unfinished customer project. Keep land, interconnection, gross versus IT capacity, phased rent, restricted debt proceeds, and conditional construction-overrun support distinct. Report only.

observations.content: A project affiliate owns approximately 75 acres at the site. The project has approvals for 300 MW of interconnection and agreements needed for market participation. An executed 15-year customer lease covers approximately 300 gross MW, identified separately as 216 MW of critical IT load.

The leased capacity is delivered across five subphases. Rent begins separately when each designated phase reaches rack-ready completion; initial rent is targeted for October 2026 and final-phase rent for March 2027. No phase is evidenced as rack-ready at the cutoff.

The customer is responsible for qualifying construction costs above a $9.5 million-per-IT-MW allowance, but not unreasonable costs or costs caused by landlord negligence or wrongful acts. The agreed initial capital basis is $578 million.

Value recaptured by selling, leasing, or repurposing legacy mining equipment can reduce the initial capital basis by no more than $288 million. Recaptured proceeds must be deposited into the notes-proceeds account and used solely for project construction and development.

A project financing issued $2.0 billion of 6.125% senior secured notes due in 2031. Net proceeds finance remaining construction, reimburse approximately $232.5 million of prior parent capital expenditure, fund debt-service reserves, and pay fees. Lease payments support mandatory amortization.

oracle.terminal_when: The report models rent by rack-ready subphase, uses IT rather than gross megawatts for the allowance, and preserves the eligibility and use restrictions around overruns, recapture, and debt.

title: Reconcile customer acceptance, financing tranches, and guarantee scope
prompt: Build the Horizon customer-and-financing state at the cutoff. Separate accepted and pending service tranches, funded and conditional debt, escrowed proceeds, and the different triggers and releases for the parent guarantees. Report only.

observations.content: A customer agreement covers four GPU-service tranches over an average five-year term with approximately $9.7 billion of total contract value. Horizon 1 was delivered and accepted in August 2026; Horizon 2 through 4 remain targeted for later phased delivery with contractual grace periods.

Twenty percent of each tranche's contract value is paid before its delivery date and later credited against service fees after the twenty-fourth calendar month of that tranche's service term. An advance receipt is not proof that the tranche has been accepted or earned.

The $3.645 billion GPU financing contains two separate instruments under a common security framework: a $1.545 billion delayed-draw term loan at one-month SOFR plus 2.25%, and up to $2.1 billion of 5.96% senior secured notes. Both are organized in up to four tranches aligned with customer-delivery milestones and conditions precedent.

At June 30, $413 million of the delayed-draw loan was funded and $1.132 billion remained unfunded subject to conditions. $525 million of notes had been issued and $1.575 billion remained unfunded subject to conditions; issued note proceeds are released from restricted escrow only when release conditions are satisfied.

If the customer validly terminates a funded tranche and no qualified replacement is secured during the remarketing period, the parent guarantee covers allocated debt and notes net of GPU disposition proceeds plus a specified upfront customer amount. That support releases tranche by tranche on acceptance. A separate managed-services guarantee covers performance by the service provider and is expressly not a guarantee of the financing subsidiary's borrowings.

oracle.terminal_when: The report phases service and revenue by acceptance, reconciles funded versus conditional financing and escrow, and keeps remarketing and performance guarantees within their distinct triggers and scopes.
